title: Failure of Conventional Roughness Metrics in Assessing Field-Limiting Mesoscopic Topography in SRF Nb Films on Cu
authors: Eric M. Lechner, Brandi Redman, Theodore S. Cahall, Anne-Marie Valente-Feliciano
abstract: A characteristic corrugated surface morphology of Nb films on Cu is identified, with mesoscopic features comparable to the London penetration depth and coherence length, and its impact on superconducting radio frequency cavity performance metrics is examined. Magnetic field enhancement factors and superheating field suppression factors are calculated within the London model for a representative corrugated geometry. These results demonstrate that roughness trends derived from buffered chemical polished and electropolished Nb cavities do not capture the impact of nanoscale surface morphology on SRF Nb thin film performance, as even surfaces that possess low average roughness can contain geometric features that generate substantial local field enhancement and significantly suppress the Bean Livingston barrier. The influence of surface roughness on impurity diffusion is also investigated, which highlights the roles of increased surface area and local geometric confinement in modifying near surface impurity distributions. Tracking the effect of impurity diffusion on the evolution of magnetic field enhancement, we show that geometrically confined impurity distributions can mitigate nanoscale magnetic field enhancement substantially.
summary: This work analyzes how the nanoscale corrugations on superconducting Nb films impact SRF cavity performance. It shows that standard roughness measurements are insufficient because local geometric features can cause significant magnetic field enhancements. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that impurity diffusion can mitigate these detrimental nanoscale field enhancements.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the nanoscale, corrugated surface morphology of superconducting Nb films affects the performance metrics of superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavities.
main_result: Conventional roughness metrics fail to capture the impact of nanoscale features, as these features can cause substantial local field enhancement and significantly suppress the Bean-Livingston barrier, even on seemingly smooth surfaces.
method: The authors calculated magnetic field enhancement factors and superheating field suppression factors using the London model applied to a representative corrugated geometry.
model_or_system: The system is superconducting Nb thin films deposited on Cu substrates, exhibiting a characteristic corrugated surface morphology with mesoscopic features comparable to the London penetration depth and coherence length.
key_observables: Magnetic field enhancement factors, superheating field suppression factors, and near-surface impurity distributions.
important_parameters: London penetration depth, coherence length, and the scale of mesoscopic surface features.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed within the framework of the London model.
paper_structure: The paper examines the impact of the characteristic corrugated surface morphology on SRF cavity performance, calculates field enhancement/suppression factors, and investigates the role of impurity diffusion in mitigating these nanoscale magnetic field enhancements.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of local field enhancement due to geometry, which is a form of boundary condition effect, is relevant to understanding energy dissipation and boundary effects in quantum systems.
